correctness.rationale: The local update rules imply leaves have no excited state from time one onward. Two core-neighbour excitations at time t-1>=2 would require their common centre excited at time t-2, so the centre cannot be resting to excite at t>=3. A five-site iff initial motif characterizes second-update core excitation and all times through four. Explicit 9x9 and 7x7 weighted matrices count circular avoidance; their characteristic-polynomial factorizations imply the two root-sum formulas. The packaged standard-library code independently checks 597780 initial states for n=3..6 and verifies characteristic coefficients and larger trace values. This is a constructive all-size proof, not just numerical extrapolation.

value.rationale: This is a natural, complete first-hitting-time classification on an unbounded standard unicyclic graph family, not an arbitrary slice. It establishes a sharp structural four-step bound and an explicit five-site causal obstruction, then solves every labelled extinction layer by low-degree algebraic spectra. The last extinction layer is both triggered by a locally rare pattern (probability 2/2187 per five-site block) and asymptotically certain, a substantive probabilistic distinction from isolated finite brute-force tables. The leaf-induced extra wave is mathematically motivated by how degree-one vertices alter simultaneous threshold contacts without being capable of sustaining excitation.
